title: The Book's concept index
description: GENERATED by scripts/harbor-research/build_concept_index.py --write. Never hand-edited. One entry per concept the Book defines or relies on, plus three normalised fact tables (sections, floats, metaphor_passages) that every entry refers to by id rather than restating. Companion to docs/harbor-research/library-index.json, which indexes RESULTS (R1-R17) rather than ideas; an entry's library_index_ids field is derived from that file by shared \label and is never typed by hand.

generated_by.description: The script that is the only legitimate author of this file.

generator_contract.description: Regenerate-and-diff. Stated in the artifact so a hand-editor is told before they start.

harvest_rule.description: The rule that decides what is a concept, stated in one sentence, so this file and its README cannot disagree about it.

min_mentions.description: The REPEATED half of the harvest rule.

chapters.description: Derived from whitepaper/textbook.json, in chapter-number order. Never a literal list here: a ninth chapter appears the day textbook.json gains one.

prefix.description: The chapter's \pdchapterprefix, as textbook.json records it.

source.description: Repo-relative path of the chapter's top-level .tex.

files.description: Every file reached from `source` by \input/\include, minus the shared preamble (pd-pedagogy.tex and friends), which carries macros rather than prose.

missing.description: true when `source` does not exist on disk. Reported rather than skipped, so a wrong path in textbook.json is loud.

metaphor_domains.description: Every source domain the lexicon knows, sorted.

sections.description: FACT TABLE. Every \section/\subsection in the corpus, once. A mention's section is looked up here by (file, line) rather than restated 12,000 times.

line.description: 1-based source line of the sectioning command.

end.description: Last line before the next section (or EOF).

label.description: The sec:/app: \label, or null -- many subsections carry none, and that is recorded rather than invented.

floats.description: FACT TABLE. Every table/figure/xltabular/longtable, with its caption text, once. An entry's floats[] names labels; the caption is read from here.

metaphor_passages.description: FACT TABLE, and the part of this index no other tool in the repo produces. One record per paragraph, and one per section, that reaches for at least one metaphor vehicle. Computed from the PASSAGE, never from the concept that happens to sit in it -- a section's vehicle set is the union over its own paragraphs, not over the paragraphs where some one concept was mentioned.

id.description: `p:<file-stem>:<start>-<end>` for a paragraph, `s:...` for a section. Stable across runs; changes when the passage's line range changes, which is the point.

section.description: sec:/app: label of the enclosing section, or null if it has none.

vehicles.description: Every figurative vehicle found in the passage, sorted. PARSED against the lexicon's metaphor_vehicles table; a vehicle not in that table is invisible.

term.description: e.g. organ, floor, ledger, seam, symptom

domain.description: e.g. anatomy, architecture, finance, textile, medicine

mixed.description: true when two or more source domains meet in this passage. This is the mixed-metaphor finding.

cash_out.description: JUDGED, not parsed. Is the metaphor ever redeemed for a literal statement nearby?

judged.description: Always true: this field is a heuristic (a marker count and a length floor), stated so no reader mistakes it for a parse.

in_prose.description: true iff some candidate sits in running prose AND reaches for none of this passage's own vehicles. This is the only value that means 'the metaphor was actually cashed out'.

only_in_float_caption.description: true when a literal statement exists but lives in a table's or figure's CAPTION and nowhere in the prose. The specimen that motivated this index -- §1.3 of chapter 1 -- is exactly this case.

kind.description: Where the sentence sits. The distinction the specimen turns on.

label.description: The float's \label, when the sentence is inside one.

still_figurative.description: Vehicles the 'literal' sentence itself still uses. Non-empty means it did not redeem anything -- it restated the metaphor with a mechanism noun attached.

coverage.description: The honest measurement. Read it beside parser_gave_up_on; a coverage number without its exclusions is a claim, not a measurement.

parser_gave_up_on.description: Stated limits of the mechanical pass, in the artifact itself.

entries.description: One per concept, sorted by id.

id.description: Normalised surface form: lowercase, de-TeX'd, 1-4 words. The query key.

surface_forms.description: Every spelling the Book uses, including aliases folded in from the lexicon.

marks.description: Where the Book MARKS this as a term (rather than merely using it). The MARKED half of the harvest rule, with its evidence.

first_use.description: THE field a reader needs, and the anchor for \pdgloss. Two of them on purpose: the earliest mention anywhere, and the earliest in running prose. A Reader's Map table row naming a term four sections before the prose introduces it is a real first appearance but a wrong place for a gloss.

context.description: `prose`, or `float:table` / `float:figure` when the first use is inside a float.

already_marked.description: Is the first use already emphasised/defined in the source? false means the Book uses the term before it marks it.

first_in_prose.description: Same shape; null when the first mention is already in prose.

pdgloss_anchor.description: `file:line` where a \pdgloss{Term}{...} belongs: the first PROSE use.

definition.description: Where the concept is actually DEFINED, as opposed to used.

judged.description: false = PARSED: the term is emphasised inside a \begin{definition} / pdclaim{Definition} environment, or is that environment's title. true = JUDGED: it is emphasised in a sentence carrying a definitional cue ('is the', 'we call', 'denotes'). The distinction is the whole point of the field.

label.description: The def:/thm: label of the environment, when there is one.

why.description: Plain-English reason this site was called a definition. A human overrules it by editing the source, not this file.

explanation.description: JUDGED. Paragraphs that EXPLAIN the concept rather than merely use it: it appears at least twice, or the paragraph carries at least two explanation cues ('because', 'in other words', 'to see why').

open_problems.description: Where the Book says this is unresolved. PARSED when an OP-N token or an op: \label is present; JUDGED when only a prose cue ('remains open', 'we do not know') is.

op_ids.description: OP-1 .. OP-11 tokens found in the paragraph.

floats.description: Figures, plots and tables this concept appears in, by label and kind. Captions are NOT repeated here: look the label up in the top-level `floats` table.

kind.description: table/figure/xltabular/longtable, or `referenced` for a label the concept's paragraphs \ref but whose float is not in the scanned corpus.

in_caption.description: true when the concept is named in the caption, not only in the body.

references.description: The \pdcite / \cite keys attached to this concept: every key cited in a paragraph that mentions it.

key.description: The \bibitem key. check_citations.py owns whether it resolves.

sites.description: How many paragraphs attach it to this concept.

exercise_use.description: Which exercises exercise this concept, and whether their solutions name it.

kind.description: Check / Trace / Open, from the pdexercise option list.

mentions_concept.description: false means the exercise asks about the concept and the solution never names it.

library_index_ids.description: DERIVED, never typed: the library-index.json entries (R1-R17, CR, B6, label-style ids) whose claimed \labels this concept also sits under. This is the join between the two indices; it cannot go stale independently because it is recomputed on every build.

is_vehicle.description: Is this concept ITSELF a figurative vehicle?

domain.description: Its source domain, from the lexicon.

occurrences.description: Same grouped shape as `mentions`; empty when is_vehicle is false.

suppressed.description: Occurrences NOT counted as metaphor because a vehicle_literal_exceptions marker was present (a product name, a cited title, a real physical thing). Recorded rather than dropped silently, so an over-broad exception shows up in the diff.

combinations.description: Which OTHER metaphors this concept co-occurs with, at both scopes. The values are ids into metaphor_passages; the passages themselves carry the vehicles, the domains and the cash-out verdict.

mixed_sections.description: The subset of `section` where two or more domains meet.

worst_section.description: Most domains, ties broken toward never-cashed-out. Start here.

mentions.description: EVERY use site, grouped by file. A mention is (file, line): its section and whether it sits inside a float are properties of the LINE and live once in the `sections` and `floats` tables.

dropped_candidates.description: Every phrase the harvest saw and rejected, with the reason. This is what makes the coverage number honest: a miss here is countable, not silent. Promote one with concept_force_include[] in concept-index.lexicon.json.

stage.description: Which half of the harvest rule rejected it.
